extracted.intended_audience: U.S. patent examiners, patent owners, patent practitioners, and third‑party requesters involved in ex parte reexamination proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive standards from the MPEP governing citation of prior art, determination of substantial new questions of patentability, Office action content, timing, notices, extensions, and other practices specific to ex parte reexamination proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of generalized prior art citations on reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalized statements such as the prior art is “cited to show the state of the art,” “cited to show the background of the invention,” or “cited of interest” would not preclude reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such generalized or boilerplate citations do not bar the Office from conducting reexamination. The Office may conduct reexamination based on prior art that was cited but whose relevance to patentability of the claims was not discussed in any prior related Office proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portola Packaging compliance procedures (overview)
rubrics_metrics.description: Office personnel must adhere to specified procedures when determining whether prosecution of an ongoing reexamination should be terminated to comply with In re Portola Packaging.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures include ascertaining the date the grant order was mailed, determining what prior art was relied upon or cited and discussed in prior related proceedings, basing rejections only on art that was neither relied upon nor discussed previously, withdrawing rejections based solely on previously relied/u-discussed art, and terminating prosecution when remaining rejections rest entirely on previously relied/cited-discussed art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ascertain reexamination grant mailing date
rubrics_metrics.description: Ascertain that the order granting reexamination was mailed prior to November 2, 2002.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the order granting reexamination was not mailed prior to November 2, 2002, different guidance applies (see the MPEP section for reexaminations ordered on or after that date).

rubrics_metrics.name: Determine prior related proceeding art status before making rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to making any rejection in the ongoing reexamination, determine for any prior related Office proceeding what prior art was (i) relied upon to reject any claim, or (ii) cited and discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This determination is required to decide whether reexamination reuses art already considered and thereby whether Portola Packaging requires termination or withdrawal of rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit rejections to art not previously relied upon or discussed
rubrics_metrics.description: Base any and all rejections of the patent claims under reexamination at least in part on prior art that was, in any prior related Office proceeding, neither (i) relied upon to reject any claim, nor (ii) cited and its relevance to patentability of any claim discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reexamination rejections should incorporate new or previously unconsidered aspects of prior art; relying solely on previously relied-upon or discussed art may contravene Portola Packaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdraw rejections based only on previously relied/cited-and-discussed art
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdraw any rejections based only on prior art that was, in any prior related Office proceeding, previously either (i) relied upon to reject any claim, or (ii) cited and its relevance to patentability of any claim discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a rejection in reexamination depends solely on art already litigated/decided in prior Office proceedings, that rejection must be withdrawn to comply with Portola Packaging.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminate prosecution when only rejections rest on previously considered art
rubrics_metrics.description: Terminate the prosecution of any reexamination in which the only remaining rejections are entirely based on prior art that was, in any prior related Office proceeding, previously (i) relied upon to reject any claim, and/or (ii) cited and its relevance to patentability of a claim discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before terminating, the Director may search for new art to determine whether a substantial new question of patentability exists (see 35 U.S.C. 303 and 305).

rubrics_metrics.name: Director may search for new art before termination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO may conduct a search for new art to determine whether a substantial new question of patentability exists prior to terminating the prosecution of any ongoing reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 35 U.S.C. 303 and 35 U.S.C. 305 (reexamination conducted according to initial examination procedures), suggesting the Director may conduct a search during reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle unusual fact patterns via CRU or TC Director
rubrics_metrics.description: In unusual fact patterns, the reexamination should be brought to the attention of the Central Reexamination Unit (CRU) or Technology Center (TC) Director who will determine the appropriate action to be taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include situations where prior art was discussed before but other evidence shows the examiner did not appreciate issues raised, or where translations/information differ from what was previously considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: New portions of a previously cited reference may create SNQ; mere new interpretation does not
rubrics_metrics.description: If a prior prosecution discussed only select information from a reference (e.g., a textbook) and a reexamination request relies on other portions that actually teach what claims require, it may be appropriate to order/rely on reexamination. However, a reexamination request that merely provides a new interpretation of a reference already previously relied upon or discussed by the Office does not create a substantial new question of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should check file history (e.g., IDS requirements, 37 CFR 1.98(a)(2)(ii)) to see which portions were previously considered; new, substantive portions may justify reexamination, but reinterpretation alone usually will not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previously discussed but improperly characterized references may justify reexamination if corrected
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an examiner discussed a reference in a prior Office proceeding but did not reject (or thought it did not qualify as prior art), a reexamination request explaining how and why the reference actually does qualify as prior art may be appropriate to order/conduct reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request could: verify the date of the reference; undermine sufficiency of a 37 CFR 1.131 declaration by showing inaccuracies; or explain correct filing date where not previously addressed. Case law (e.g., Heinl v. Godici) supports reexamination when prior art status is newly established.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign language prior art translation may create SNQ
rubrics_metrics.description: If a foreign language prior art reference was cited and discussed in any prior Office proceeding but never completely and accurately translated into English during the original prosecution, a complete and accurate translation submitted in a reexamination request may be appropriate to order and/or conduct reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reexamination request should explain why the more complete/accurate translation actually teaches what is required by the claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of cumulative references
rubrics_metrics.description: A cumulative reference that is repetitive of a prior art reference previously applied or discussed may be prohibited from supporting reexamination if it substantially reiterates verbatim the teachings of the earlier reference, even if title or citation differs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such exclusion is expected to be rare because most references add information or present teachings differently; examiners should assess whether the reference merely repeats previous teachings verbatim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required wording when terminating prosecution under Portola Packaging
rubrics_metrics.description: If prosecution of an ongoing reexamination is terminated under Portola Packaging, the Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate should state: 'The prosecution of this reexamination is terminated based on In re Portola Packaging, Inc., 110 F.3d 786, 42 USPQ2d 1295 (Fed. Cir. 1997). No patentability determination has been made in this reexamination proceeding.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a rejection is withdrawn to comply with Portola, the Office action withdrawing such rejection should explicitly state that the rejection(s) based upon _______ is/are withdrawn in view of In re Portola Packaging and that no patentability determination of the claims in view of such prior art has been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Res judicata and collateral estoppel in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims finally held invalid by a Federal Court after all appeals will be withdrawn from consideration and not reexamined during reexamination. Where a Court decision did not invalidate claims but decided issues applicable to the claims, collateral estoppel may be applied in reexamination to resolve that issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consult MPEP §§ 2242 and 2286 for Office policy when a Federal Court decision on the merits exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's duty to make a thorough study and investigation (37 CFR 1.104(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: On taking up an application for examination or a patent in reexamination, the examiner shall make a thorough study thereof and shall make a thorough investigation of the available prior art relating to the subject matter of the claimed invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examination shall be complete with respect both to compliance with applicable statutes/rules and to the patentability of the invention as claimed, as well as matters of form (unless otherwise indicated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office action must state reasons for adverse action and assist parties (37 CFR 1.104(a)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant, or in reexamination both the patent owner and the requester, will be notified of the examiner's action. The reasons for any adverse action or any objection or requirement will be stated in an Office action and such information or references will be given as may be useful in aiding the parties to judge the propriety of continuing prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions should be sufficiently informative to allow parties to understand and respond to the grounds of rejection or objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: International-type search availability
rubrics_metrics.description: An international-type search will be made in all national applications filed on and after June 1, 1978. Any national application may also have an international-type search report prepared at national examination upon written request and payment of the fee (§ 1.21(e)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PTO does not require a formal international-type search report for obtaining a search fee refund in a later-filed international application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of examiner's action and timing of form issues
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's action will be complete as to all matters, except that in appropriate circumstances (e.g., misjoinder, fundamental defects) the action may be limited to such matters before further action is made. Matters of form need not be raised until a claim is found allowable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners may focus on core issues first and defer purely formal matters until claim allowability is being addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for rejecting claims for novelty/obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention is not patentable, the claims will be rejected. When rejecting for want of novelty or for obviousness, the examiner must cite the best references at his or her command, designate the particular part relied on when a reference is complex, clearly explain the pertinency of each reference if not apparent, and specify each rejected claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate specific portions of complex references 'as nearly as practicable' and explain how the references apply to each rejected claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reliance on admissions and facts within examiner knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: In rejecting claims the examiner may rely upon admissions by the applicant, or the patent owner in reexamination, as to any matter affecting patentability and may rely upon facts within his or her knowledge (subject to applicable rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When relying on facts within personal knowledge of an Office employee, the data shall be as specific as possible and, if called for by the applicant, supported by that employee's affidavit (subject to contradiction/explanation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 102(e)/(f)/(g) prior art in 103 rejections and common-ownership exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject matter developed by another person which qualifies as prior art only under 35 U.S.C. 102(e), (f) or (g) may be used as prior art under 35 U.S.C. 103 against a claimed invention unless the entire rights to the subject matter and the claimed invention were commonly owned by the same person or subject to an obligation of assignment at the time the claimed invention was made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check ownership/assignment facts before relying on such references in an obviousness rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory invention registration waiver precludes claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims in an original application naming an inventor will be rejected as being precluded by a waiver in a published statutory invention registration naming that inventor if the same subject matter is claimed in the application and the statutory invention registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For reissue applications, similar rejections apply where the reissue seeks subject matter not covered by earlier issued claims and which was the same subject matter waived in the statutory invention registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation information requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If domestic patents are cited, their numbers, dates, and names of patentees will be stated. For domestic patent application publications, publication number/date/names of applicants will be stated. For foreign published applications/patents, nationality/country, numbers/dates, and patentee names and other data necessary to identify the documents will be furnished. For printed publications, author, title, date, pages/plates, and place of publication or where a copy can be found will be given.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where only part of a foreign document is involved, identify particular pages/sheets containing the parts relied upon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specificity when relying on Office employee personal knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: When a rejection is based on facts within the personal knowledge of an Office employee, the data shall be as specific as possible, and the reference must be supported, when called for by the applicant, by the affidavit of such employee; the affidavit is subject to contradiction or explanation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure supporting affidavits are available and specific when relying on personal-knowledge facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasons for allowance documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes the record does not make clear his or her reasons for allowing a claim, the examiner may set forth such reasoning. The reasons shall be incorporated into an Office action rejecting other claims or be the subject of a separate communication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The applicant or patent owner may file a statement commenting on reasons for allowance within specified time; examiner's failure to respond to such a statement does not imply anything.

rubrics_metrics.name: First ex parte action should establish issues and warn patent owner (form paragraph 22.04)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's first ex parte action on the merits should be the primary action to establish the issues between the examiner and the patent owner. It should caution the patent owner that a complete response should be made since the next action is expected to be final and that 37 CFR 1.116(b) will be strictly enforced after final action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 22.04 (Papers To Be Submitted in Response to Action - Ex Parte Reexamination) language is appropriate for inclusion in the first Office action; it explains that submissions after the next Office action will be governed by 37 CFR 1.116 and 41.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of dependent claims in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If an unamended base patent claim (a claim appearing in the reexamination as it appears in the patent) has been rejected or canceled, any claim which is directly or indirectly dependent thereon should be confirmed or allowed if the dependent claim is otherwise allowable. The dependent claim should not be objected to or rejected merely because it depends on a rejected or canceled patent claim, and no rewriting into independent form is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a new base claim (not appearing in the patent) has been canceled, a claim depending thereon should be rejected as indefinite. If a new base claim or an amended patent claim is rejected, a dependent claim should be objected to if otherwise patentable and require rewriting in independent form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special dispatch requirement and time goals (35 U.S.C. 305)
rubrics_metrics.description: All reexamination proceedings, including appeals, will be conducted with special dispatch within the Office. The examiner's first action on the merits should be completed within 1 month of the filing date of the requester's reply (37 CFR 1.535) or the patent owner's statement (37 CFR 1.530) if no other requester, and mailing should occur within 6 weeks after the appropriate filing or due date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases involved in litigation have priority over other cases. Reexaminations not involved in litigation have priority over other non-litigation cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and content requirements for Office Actions (first action)
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner's first Office action must be a statement of the examiner's position, typed, and sufficiently detailed that the second Office action can properly be made a final action. The first action must clearly set forth the pertinency and manner of applying cited prior art to the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner may cut-and-paste claim charts included in the request but must carefully review them; later actions must address all patent owner responses. If claims are patentable, indicate why in a manner similar to reasons for allowance. Treat inappropriate arguments per 37 CFR 1.552(c). Given finality of reexamination, actions must be thorough and complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules for changing the title during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally the title will not need to be changed during reexamination. If change is necessary, patent owner should be notified early. If all claims are found patentable and a Notice of Intent to Issue Ex Parte Reexamination Certificate has been or is to be mailed, a change to the title by the examiner may only be done by a formal Examiner's Amendment; merely initialing the change is NOT permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notify patent owner as early as possible when a title change is necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice for examiner-initiated discussions and amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner may indicate that a discussion with the patent owner's representative may result in agreement to place the reexamination in condition for issuing a NIRC and will telephone the representative within about 2 weeks. Any resulting amendment may be made by the patent owner's attorney/agent or by the examiner in an examiner's amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When extensive amendments are necessary it is preferable that the patent owner's attorney/agent file them to provide a better file record including arguments required by 37 CFR 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel review conference process
rubrics_metrics.description: After an examiner has determined the reexamination is ready for an Office action, the examiner will inform the CRU SPE or TC QAS of intent to issue the Office action; the CRU SPE/TC QAS will convene a panel review conference to review patentability pursuant to MPEP § 2271.01.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the conference confirms the examiner's preliminary decision to reject and/or allow, the proposed Office action shall be issued and signed by the examiner with two other conferees initialing as 'conferee' to indicate presence. If not confirmed, the examiner will reevaluate and issue an appropriate Office action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content examples in sample Office action (include statutory quotation and clear explanations)
rubrics_metrics.description: A sample first Office action may include quotations of statutory provisions (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 103) forming basis for obviousness rejections, explicit explanations of how references combine to make claims obvious, and statements regarding issues outside the scope of reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include clear explanation why claims are rejected or allowed, identification of cited references and their roles, and advice to patentees about related options (e.g., reissue) for issues not within reexamination scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened statutory response periods in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: A shortened statutory period of 2 months will be set for response to Office actions in reexaminations except as follows: where the reexamination results from a court order or litigation is stayed for reexamination, the shortened statutory period will be set at 1 month. Additional 1-month shortened periods may be approved in particular litigation circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement at the end of the Office action indicating approval of a one-month or thirty-days shortened statutory period (signed by appropriate official) designates such approval. This 1-month policy does NOT apply to the 2-month period for filing a statement under 37 CFR 1.530 (set by 35 U.S.C. 304). Where a reexamination was stayed for a co-pending reissue abandoned thereafter, actions after the stay will set a 1-month shortened statutory period unless a longer period is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing procedures and transmittal forms (PTOL-465)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte reexamination forms are structured for PALM printing of identifying information and mailing addresses; only the first patent owner's address is printed where multiple owners. A transmittal form PTOL-465 is provided for each partial patent owner and for third-party requesters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All actions in a third-party requester ex parte reexamination will have a copy mailed to the third-party requester. Use PTOL-465 to provide copies to third-party requesters and partial patent owners; it also helps determine number of copies to mail and permits use of window envelopes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension of time rules in ex parte reexamination (37 CFR 1.550(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The time for taking any action by a patent owner in an ex parte reexamination proceeding will be extended only for sufficient cause and for a reasonable time specified. Any request for extension must be filed on or before the day action is due and must be accompanied by the petition fee set forth in § 1.17(g); mere filing does not effect extension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for extension will be considered only after the decision to grant or deny reexamination is mailed (requests filed before that decision will be denied). The provisions of 37 CFR 1.136(a) and (b) are NOT applicable to ex parte reexamination. Except for an automatic 1-month extension granted upon filing a first timely response to a final Office action, all other extension requests must be filed under 37 CFR 1.550(c) and will be decided by the Director of the CRU or TC conducting the reexamination. Evaluation of sufficient cause must balance giving the patent owner a fair opportunity to present arguments and the statute's requirement for special dispatch (35 U.S.C. 305).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of certificates of mailing/transmission and Express Mail
rubrics_metrics.description: The certificate of mailing and the certificate of transmission procedures (37 CFR 1.8) and the Express Mail mailing procedure (37 CFR 1.10) may be used to file a request for extension of time, as well as any other paper in a pending ex parte reexamination proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard mailing/transmission proof procedures accepted in PTO practice apply to reexamination filings (see MPEP § 2266).
